title: DECISION: burnOnRead explicitly cannot be relied on across receiptSharing boundary
description:
Choice: The burnOnRead field definition explicitly states that when the recipient's effective receiptSharing preference is false, no readAt signal reaches the sender, so burnOnRead is not guaranteed to trigger — and senders MUST NOT rely on it for confidentiality when the recipient's preference is unknown.

Why good: burnOnRead sounds like a confidentiality guarantee but its trigger depends on a readAt event that the receiptSharing opt-out suppresses. Documenting this interaction prevents implementors and users from assuming burnOnRead provides end-to-end deletion guarantees when receipt sharing is disabled. The MUST NOT is the right strength — it closes the false-security trap.

Alternatives avoided: Leaving the interaction undocumented (implementor confusion, false security assumptions); making burnOnRead override receiptSharing (would break the privacy opt-out from the other direction); removing burnOnRead entirely (loses a legitimate feature for opted-in users).
